1. Testing with Unit tests is not enough. Please test this with the Redfish Service validator, please refer to https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/TESTING.md and do actually setup subscription on a running instance and show what it sent.
2. I doubt (99% sure) it's going to work in the way you expect. The way DBus subscription works is, BMCWeb listens for DBus events along with the LogService, so when a source service sends an event, both services receive it at the same time, and at this time, the LogEntry ID is not even assigned yet.
Please review the redfish checklist.  At a minimum you've missed both the testing requirement and the documentation requirement for your newly added properties.

1. Thanks for pointing out! I have performed an end to end testing on QEMU with a proper subscription setup and event log sent out, the test plan has been updated with the data.
2. `LogEntryId` passed to formatEventLogEntry does contain a valid id which points to the correct LogEntry, verified this finding in my testing, please check the testing output.

I have gone through the Redfish checklist to ensure we meet all the requirements listed here:
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/REDFISH_CHECKLIST.md

This function is formatting common parts of the Event (https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Event.v1_4_0.json) and LogEntry (https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/LogEntry.v1_21_0.json) both.

what you are doing here is, you're going to store the URL under the LogEntry property of both Event and LogEntry structures, while only Event has it and the LogEntry has the "@odata.id" field on the top level and not under the LogEntry property that do not exist.
I'm wrong here, it's only called from the subscription.cpp.

The LogEntry property was added to the Event structure starting version 1.7.0 (see https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Event.v1_7_0.json), BMCWeb uses version 1.4.0 (https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/40083a9a875e33b367e88ea9a21ecc35177bfc94/redfish-core/src/subscription.cpp#L250), so you also need to bump a version of the structure.
Since you're changing a version, you need to see what changed between the versions and at least move data from deprecated fields to their replacements (like Severity which was deprecated in 1.5.0 to MessageSeverity replaced it, note that MessageSeverity is the Health type and Severity was a String), and potentially add new required fields should any new required fields were added.

Done - I have now bumped the event schema version to the correct version which contains LogEntry field, also verified that all the mandatory fields are populated and deprecated fields (eg: `Severity`) are removed.

Please deduplicate this code.  It's very similar.

Also, buffer() is not required.

Done - code de-duplication has been done, however buffer is still needed for explicit conversion to nlohmann::json, otherwise unit tests fail with
` no known conversion for argument 1 from ‘boost::urls::url’ to ‘nlohmann::json_abi_v3_12_0::basic_json<>'`

Error handling looks like it will write invalid here.

yes, if I don't send this value, the issue of invalid severity will be silently swallowed. 
Also, severity is not a mandatory value, I don't want event push to fail because of Invalid severity.

> invalid severity will be silently swallowed.

This isn't true.  It will write "invalid" to the json output.
even if I don't send the Invalid value, it will? How so?
Please look at the code.  You either forgot a return or an else here if you're doing what I'm expecting.
as written, if it == Invalid, the only difference in flow is that it prints a warning.  It still calls the same code.

No, I don't want the code to return, if it received an invalid, I'm logging a warning and continuing to push the event. This is because "MessageSeverity" is not a mandatory value.

To answer your question, why explicit check here, this is because "Severity" is a string being populated from message registry, whereas "MessageSeverity" is based off Resource::Health enum, while translating the messageSeverity string to Resource::Health enum value, it could potentially get a Invalid back if no mapping was found within the enum. This is a possibility for "MessageSeverity" field not "Severity" field within the json, therefore needs explicit handling.

Please note - 
Old code is populating  logEntryJson["Severity"]        //<String>
The patch is populating logEntryJson["MessageSeverity"] //<Resource::Health enum>

They are different fields with different data types.
Done

not sure why this was marked done?  We're parsing a generated string, into an enum, just to generate the string again.

Sure, you've changed Severity -> MessageSeverity, but they're both coming from the same source and have the same type.

>  if it received an invalid, I'm logging a warning and continuing to push the event.

This is not how we handle most errors. if there's an internal error, we log it and stop the flow.


> because "Severity" is a string being populated from message registry, whereas "MessageSeverity" is based off Resource::Health enum

Right, so you've deleted Severity as a property?  Did that show up in your testing?

>Sure, you've changed Severity -> MessageSeverity, but they're both coming from the same source and have the same type.

Are you suggesting we don't need to perform any enum lookup , it can be directly assigned from the string message->MessageSeverity.

> Right, so you've deleted Severity as a property? Did that show up in your testing?

Yes, during the testing the new field `MessageSeverity` showed up in the Json payload returned by bmcweb with `Severity` being removed. Test plan captures and shows the payload in [4].

I have now amended my logic to populate MessageSeverity in the same way as Severity, i.e through direct string assignment.

I have also left Severity field as-is to prevent any regression issues.
I have verified this change in my testing (detailed test steps included in the change description) as well as captured it in the test log to ensure both the fields are correctly populated. Additionally, I have run unit tests and redfish validator to ensure it passes.
Done
